checks.name: observer-is-constructed-once-and-cached
checks.summary: the no-per-request-walk claim is measured, not asserted by construction: the test copies every assembled bundle member into a temporary tree, constructs the observer, DELETES the tree (and asserts the deletion actually happened, so the fixture cannot be vacuous), then reads the surface again and asserts the same release version, bundle digest, assembly instant and condition count come back. A per-request walk would have failed or changed its answer. Construction refuses a blank root, a blank repository, a blank environment class and a zero assembly instant, so there is no default root and no clock read; every timestamp in these tests is the injected time.Unix(1700000500, 0) UTC.

checks.name: not-configured-is-distinguishable
checks.summary: with no observer attached the read returns application.ErrReleaseObserverNotConfigured, which the route maps to 503 with the explicit code release_observer_not_configured, and the returned view carries no release version, no bundle digest and zero conditions: a process that was not given an explicit release source root reports no version at all rather than guessing one. The read is gated by callerActor(ctx, RoleOwner) exactly as the other owner reads are: an unauthenticated context and a RoleRunner context are both refused.

checks.name: rollback-target-and-bounded-retention
checks.summary: after two gated promotions the surface reports Route.PreviousStableDigest as the rollback target with rollback_available true. After one rollback the target is empty and rollback_available is false, because release.Router.Rollback is monotonic and clears the forward pointer as it moves, and a second consecutive rollback is refused with 'no previous stable route'. The recorded RollbackHistory entry carries repository, from, to, reason and the injected timestamp. The retention read goes through the existing bounded u.RequirementsPage with limit application.MaxPageSize and reports requirements_examined, scan_bounded true, page_size 100 and more_requirements_exist; a Requirement whose StableSnapshot references the target is found and named. Measured impedance mismatch, reported in the payload rather than hidden: the route names a candidate digest while domain.StableReleaseSnapshot records a ReleaseID and a BundleDigest, so the comparison is over both of those fields and rollback_target_compared_against names them. A process that recorded no route answers recorded false with the note 'no route recorded', with every route field left empty.

checks.summary: component edge measured effect. ci/components.json gained exactly one declaration: component application's dependencies now lists release, and nothing else in that file changed (git diff: 2 insertions, 1 deletion, the deletion being the reflowed closing bracket of the dependencies array). The declaration and the real non-test import are in the same commit, because ci.VerifyNoUnjustifiedEdges rejects a declared edge that is not derived from any import, literal or check target. ci/key-closure.json was regenerated with devbox run --pure -- make key-closure and git diff --exit-code on it is clean afterwards. Measured consequence, wider than 'application and api': seven component closures changed, api, application, control-plane, reconciler, runner, store-firestore and store-memory, because every one of them depends transitively on application. Each of those seven now hashes internal/release/**, and the five that did not already reach contracts also gained contracts/**, contracts/release-contract/** and contracts/schemas/release-contract.json. The accepted side effect is that a contract or release edit now invalidates those component keys, which is what V2-045 intended: selective CI must select application and api when internal/release changes.
